label: H.R. 10329
title: Combating Foreign Threats to Main Street Act of 2026

items.snippet: This bill requires the Small Business Administration, in consultation with appropriate agencies, to develop and publish educational materials about foreign adversary conduct that poses material harm to small businesses.

This bill requires the Small Business Administration, in consultation with appropriate agencies, to develop and publish educational materials about foreign adversary conduct that poses material harm to small businesses.

The educational materials must (1) describe the conduct that poses such harm, (2) identify best practices for small businesses to protect sensitive information and supply chains, and (3) provide guidance for cybersecurity and data protection.

lobbying.caption: From Senate lobbying disclosures (LD-2). A filing mentions this bill; it does not show what was asked for, which side the client took, or any contact with this member. Reported amounts cover the whole filing, not this bill alone.
lobbying.amount_note: Amounts are the income or expenses reported on the whole LD-2 filing, not money spent on this bill.

caption: This shows who the bill names and who lobbied on it. It does not show who gains or loses, and lobbying can be for or against a bill.

W000816.label: Overlap, not proof of influence.
W000816.caption: Money from this member's itemized individual donors (over $200) whose self-reported employer falls in an industry that also has a client lobbying on this bill. Correlation only; not a quid pro quo. Donors give to campaigns for many reasons, and a lobbying client may have opposed the bill.
W000816.note: None of the lobbying clients on this bill matched an industry rule, so there is nothing to compare.
